# SilentMesh Systems

> Kernel-level cyber deception for OT/ICS and converged IT/OT networks. Linux
> eBPF at the traffic-control layer redirects industrial protocol traffic to
> protocol-accurate decoys while the real controllers stay untouched.

Motto: Deceive, never disrupt.
Contact: founder@silentmesh.me
Canonical site: https://www.silentmesh.me/

## Disambiguation

SilentMesh Systems (this company, silentmesh.me) is an industrial
cybersecurity company working on OT/ICS deception at the Linux kernel level.

It is unrelated to Silent Mesh (silentmesh.net), a separate company working on
acoustic FPV drone detection. The two share a name and nothing else.

## What the product does

- Places decoy industrial controllers on a plant network: Modbus/TCP, S7comm,
  IEC 60870-5-104, DNP3 and OPC UA, plus a decoy Windows file share (SMB) and a
  read-only SNMP responder.
- A small eBPF program attached with TCX (Linux 6.6 and later) hands
  connections aimed at the decoy host's industrial ports to the decoys. Traffic
  to any other address or port is passed untouched; it never sits between an
  HMI and a controller.
- Fails open. If the software stops for any reason the kernel releases the
  hook; if it freezes, a kernel lease lapses within about 9 seconds. Tested on
  every code change on kernels 6.6 to 7.2.
- Non-interference: 20,000 random plant packets per kernel come back byte for
  byte, none dropped, on every code change.
- Positioned as additive, not a replacement: a high-fidelity alert source for
  the SIEM, SOAR or monitoring stack an operator already runs.

## What it does not do and does not claim

- It does not claim decoys are undetectable. The defensible claim is a stated
  fingerprint-resistance threshold, what it tests, and what it does not test.
- It does not block, filter or enforce. It deceives and reports.
- Published performance figures come from a single environment across four
  trials and are not a claim about every deployment.
- It is pre-pilot. There are no production customer deployments to cite.

## Pages

- [Home](https://www.silentmesh.me/): what the product is, how it works, what it never does, evidence with the test behind each figure, what is not done yet.
- [Blog](https://www.silentmesh.me/blog/): engineering log index.
- [Pilot](https://www.silentmesh.me/pilot/): one segment, monitor-only first, 30 days, seven pass criteria agreed in writing before anything connects.
- [Security](https://www.silentmesh.me/security/): guarantees and how each is tested, release gate, known gaps, vulnerability reporting.
- [Our Go fuzzing ran nothing, and every check was green](https://www.silentmesh.me/blog/fuzzing-that-ran-nothing/): engineering log. A failing command substitution in a shell for-list is not caught by set -e; the fuzz step now fails if zero targets ran.
- [We built decoy fingerprint tests that could not fail](https://www.silentmesh.me/blog/tests-that-could-not-fail/): engineering log. How a self-check mode proved three of eight fingerprint probes were measuring the probe rather than the decoy, and what changed.
